dish_name: Pork with Black Bean Sauce and Peppers
instructions: Slice the pork across the grain into thin strips about 1/4 inch thick. Transfer them into a bowl.
Add 1 1/2 tbsp rice wine, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 3/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper and 1/4 cup water to the pork. Work it with your hands for 2 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Let it sit for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the red and green peppers into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Slice the white and light green parts of 4 scallions into 1 inch pieces and thinly slice the rest of the bunch for the end. Mince the garlic and 1 tbsp of the ginger.
In a small bowl, stir 2 tsp of the cornstarch into the broth until smooth. Set it next to the stove.
Just before cooking, add the remaining 2 tsp cornstarch and the sesame oil to the pork and toss until every slice is coated.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add half the pork in a single layer and let it sit for 1 minute. Stir and cook 1 minute, until the slices are pale and lightly browned at the edges. Transfer to a plate.
Repeat with another 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the pork.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan over medium-high heat. Add the peppers and stir for 2 minutes, until they brighten and start to soften.
Add the scallion pieces, garlic and ginger. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell the garlic.
Add the black bean sauce and stir for 15 seconds. Stir the broth again and pour it in. Let it bubble for 1 minute, until it thickens and coats a spoon.

Return the pork and any juices to the pan. Toss for 1 minute. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick slice. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Scatter the sliced scallions over the top and serve straight from the pan.
method_notes: The lead is a quick Sichuan-style stir-fry: pork marinated in wine, soy and cornstarch, set aside, then ginger, garlic and scallion, and the black bean sauce stirred in at the end. It uses hot fresh chilies and a dark soy sauce; here the chilies become red and green bell peppers to keep the base mild, and the dark soy is left out. A small amount of thickened broth comes from the Heart and Stroke Foundation's pork and black bean stir-fry with bell peppers (no rating shown) so the dish has a sauce. Foodelicacy's pork with colored peppers confirms the order: pork first, then peppers, then the black bean mixture.
